goal: Improve evals, observability, and robustness across the Support Bundle Investigator: build a real eval scorecard across all scenarios, add AI replay/cassette evals, expand scenario corpus for newer investigators, enrich trace.json with seed/retrieval/confidence telemetry, add a debug mode with per-finding provenance, add cost/latency/model summaries for AI runs, and add robustness tests for corrupt/partial/oversized bundles, stress/perf benchmarks, and sensitive-data leakage.

steps.title: Expand eval scorecard: add ghost-service and multi-namespace-retrieval to GOLDEN_EXPECTATIONS
steps.description: In `test/golden/expectations.ts`, add ScenarioExpectation entries for the existing `ghost-service` and `multi-namespace-retrieval` fixture scenarios. These scenarios already have fixture data in `test/fixtures/scenarios/` but no golden expectations. Define `topFindingMustMatch`, `topFindingSeverity`, `topFindingMinConfidence`, `mustCiteEvidence`, `mustNotHallucinate`, `rootCauseMustMatch`, and `mustMentionIdentifiers` for each. The existing `golden-eval.test.ts` auto-iterates `GOLDEN_EXPECTATIONS`, so these will be tested automatically. Run the pipeline heuristic-only (noAi: true) against both scenarios first in a scratch test to determine the actual finding patterns, then set expectations to match. Follow the existing expectation pattern style exactly.

steps.title: Add new scenario fixtures: network-policy-deny and node-taint-memory-pressure
steps.description:
Create two new fixture scenario directories under `test/fixtures/scenarios/`:

1. `network-policy-deny/` — a scenario where a NetworkPolicy denies all egress from a pod, causing connection failures. Include: analysis.json with a connectivity warning, pod YAML with labels matching the policy, a NetworkPolicy YAML with deny-all egress, events with connection timeouts, and a pod log showing connection refused errors. This exercises the network-policy-investigator.

2. `node-taint-memory-pressure/` — a scenario where a pod is Pending because the node has a MemoryPressure taint and the pod has no toleration. Include: analysis.json with scheduling failure, pod YAML in Pending phase with no tolerations, node YAML with MemoryPressure taint, FailedScheduling events, and a log with scheduling warnings. This exercises the kubernetes-investigator's pending-pod path.

Follow the exact directory structure of existing fixtures (analysis.json, cluster-resources/, version.yaml). Add golden expectations for both in `test/golden/expectations.ts`.

steps.title: Add new scenario fixture: helm-release-failure
steps.description: Create `test/fixtures/scenarios/helm-release-failure/` for a Helm release in a failed/pending-install state. Include: analysis.json with a Helm failure analyzer, a helm-release JSON file (under `cluster-resources/helm/` or equivalent) with status FAILED, pod YAML showing CrashLoopBackOff from a bad Helm values override, events with FailedMount or similar, and logs with Helm-related errors. Add a golden expectation entry. This demonstrates Helm release investigation coverage introduced in the helm-parser.

steps.title: Build eval scorecard JSON reporter and summary test
steps.description: Create `test/golden/scorecard.ts` that exports a `generateScorecard(report: EvalReport): string` function which renders a human-readable Markdown table and a machine-readable JSON summary of all scenario results. The table should have columns: Scenario, Pass/Fail, Score%, Top Finding, Expected Pattern, Confidence, Evidence Count, Heuristic/AI. Also create `test/golden/__tests__/scorecard.test.ts` that runs all GOLDEN_EXPECTATIONS scenarios, builds the EvalReport via `buildEvalReport`, generates the scorecard, and asserts: (1) the scorecard is valid Markdown, (2) every scenario row is present, (3) overallScore > 0.9. This formalizes the eval as a regression gate.

steps.title: AI cassette eval test: replay-based golden eval
steps.description:
Create `test/golden/__tests__/cassette-eval.test.ts` that tests AI investigation using pre-recorded cassettes. Steps:
1. Create a `test/fixtures/cassettes/` directory with a hand-crafted `cassettes.json` file containing realistic (but synthetic) LLM responses for at least 2 scenarios (bad-image-tag, missing-secret-crashloop).
2. The test sets `SBI_AI_MODE=replay`, constructs a CassetteRecorder in replay mode, loads from the fixture cassettes, and verifies: (a) each cassette can be replayed by seed key, (b) replayed findings pass basic schema validation, (c) replayed findings integrated with heuristic findings still pass golden expectations.
3. Test that when a cassette is missing for a seed, the system degrades gracefully (returns empty findings, no throw).
This proves AI replay infrastructure works end-to-end without requiring real API keys.

steps.title: Enrich InvestigationTrace with seed, retrieval, and confidence telemetry
steps.description:
Extend the `TraceStep` interface in `src/pipeline/trace.ts` with optional telemetry fields:
- `seedCount?: number` — number of seeds generated (on the 'investigate' step)
- `seedCategories?: Record<string, number>` — breakdown by category
- `retrievalStats?: { graphChunks: number; lexicalChunks: number; semanticChunks: number; mergedChunks: number }` — per-step retrieval breakdown
- `confidenceStats?: { min: number; max: number; mean: number; median: number }` — confidence distribution of findings
- `hypothesisStats?: { generated: number; verified: number; converted: number }` — hypothesis layer counters

Also add a top-level `InvestigationTrace.metadata?: Record<string, unknown>` for extensible key-value telemetry.

Update `analyzeBundlePipeline` in `src/pipeline/analyze.ts` to populate these fields from `investigationResult.metadata` and the parsed artifact counts. Ensure the existing trace JSON serialization tests still pass. Update `test/e2e/__tests__/scenarios.test.ts` trace tests to verify the new fields are present and sensible.

steps.title: Add per-finding provenance to Finding type and populate in investigators
steps.description:
Add an optional `provenance?: FindingProvenance` field to the `Finding` interface in `src/types/finding.ts`. Define `FindingProvenance` as:
```typescript
interface FindingProvenance {
  investigator: string;  // e.g. 'kubernetes', 'log', 'config', 'service', 'network-policy', 'hypothesis', 'ai', 'graph-causal'
  seedId?: string;       // the seed that triggered this finding
  seedSource?: string;   // seed.source value
  generatedAt: string;   // ISO timestamp
  mergedFrom?: string[]; // IDs of findings absorbed during dedup
  hypothesisFamily?: string; // normalizeIssueFamilyForPass1 result
  confidenceDelta?: number;  // change from raw to verified confidence
}
```
Populate `provenance` in each investigator (kubernetes, log, config, service, network-policy), in the hypothesis converter, in the AI investigator, and in the graph causal finding builder. In the orchestrator's merge passes, populate `mergedFrom` when findings are absorbed. In the verifier, compute and set `confidenceDelta`. Add a `--debug` flag check: when `PipelineOptions.debug` is true, provenance is included in the JSON report output; otherwise it's stripped. Add unit tests verifying provenance fields are set on findings from each investigator path.

steps.title: Add AI cost/latency/model summary to trace and report
Add --debug CLI flag that emits enriched trace and provenance
steps.description:
Add a `--debug` flag to the CLI in `src/cli/runner.ts` (via Commander). When set, it:
1. Sets `PipelineOptions.debug = true` and `PipelineOptions.verbose = true`.
2. After pipeline completes, writes an enriched `trace.json` that includes the new telemetry fields (seed stats, retrieval stats, confidence stats, AI summary) and finding provenance.
3. Writes a `provenance.json` file alongside the trace containing each finding's full provenance chain.
4. Logs a summary table to stderr showing: per-finding investigator, seed, confidence delta, and merge history.

Update `src/cli/output.ts` with `writeProvenanceFile()` function. Add a CLI integration test in `src/cli/__tests__/runner.test.ts` that verifies the --debug flag triggers the extra output files.

steps.title: Robustness: corrupt and partial bundle tests
steps.description:
Create `test/integration/__tests__/robustness.test.ts` with tests for:
1. **Corrupt archive** — a file that is not valid gzip (random bytes with .tar.gz extension). Assert `extractBundle` throws a clear error, not an unhandled crash.
2. **Truncated archive** — a valid .tar.gz header but truncated mid-stream. Assert extraction throws gracefully.
3. **Empty archive** — a valid .tar.gz with zero entries. Assert pipeline completes with 0 findings and no crash.
4. **Missing expected files** — a bundle with only an analysis.json and no cluster-resources/. Assert pipeline completes with partial results (analyzer findings but no resource/event/log findings).
5. **Malformed YAML/JSON** — a bundle where a pod YAML file contains invalid YAML. Assert the parser skips the bad file and continues.
6. **Binary file in bundle** — a bundle containing a .png file. Assert the profiler classifies it as 'unknown' and parsers skip it.

Create minimal fixture data programmatically in each test (using tar.c in-memory or fs writes to tmpdir).

steps.title: Robustness: oversized bundle guard test
steps.description:
Create tests in `test/integration/__tests__/robustness.test.ts` (same file as step-10) for:
1. **Oversized archive** — use the `maxSize` option on `extractBundle` with a small limit (e.g., 1KB) and a normal test bundle. Assert it throws with a clear 'exceeds maxSize' error.
2. **Large single file** — a bundle with one 5MB log file. Assert the pipeline completes without OOM (just a timing/memory sanity check).
3. **Many small files** — a bundle with 500+ tiny files. Assert profiling and parsing complete without issues.

These tests validate the extractor's maxSize guard and parser resilience to scale.

steps.title: Robustness: sensitive-data leakage tests
steps.description:
Create `test/integration/__tests__/sensitive-data.test.ts` with tests that verify no sensitive data leaks into reports or prompts:
1. **Secret values in pod env** — create a fixture pod YAML with `env` entries containing `valueFrom.secretKeyRef`. Run the pipeline. Assert that no finding's evidence.note, reasoningSummary, or recommendedAction contains the actual secret value (use a canary value like 'SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN_12345').
2. **Passwords in logs** — create a fixture log file with lines like 'Connecting with password=hunter2'. Run the pipeline. Assert the password string does not appear in any finding text or evidence note.
3. **API keys in ConfigMap** — create a fixture ConfigMap with a key named 'api-key' containing a canary token. Assert the token value does not appear in findings.
4. **Prompt safety** — when AI is enabled, build the investigation prompt from a seed against chunks that contain sensitive values. Assert the prompt's user content does not contain the canary secret values (test that the chunk content is included as-is, but the prompt grounding reminder does not extract/highlight secret values).
5. **Report output safety** — run generateMarkdownReport, generateHtmlReport, and generateJsonReport on findings from the sensitive fixture. Assert no canary values appear in any format.

This proves the system does not inadvertently surface secret data in user-facing output.

steps.title: Performance benchmark test for pipeline throughput
steps.description:
Create `test/integration/__tests__/perf-benchmark.test.ts` with a test that:
1. Creates a moderately-sized bundle (the existing pvc-pending or wrong-db-endpoint fixture).
2. Runs `analyzeBundlePipeline` with `noAi: true` and measures wall-clock time.
3. Asserts the pipeline completes in under 10 seconds (generous ceiling for CI).
4. Records per-step latency from the trace and asserts no single step exceeds 5 seconds.
5. Runs the pipeline 3 times and asserts the variance in total time is within 2x (no pathological outliers).

This gives a regression gate on pipeline performance. The test should use `{ timeout: 30000 }` in vitest to avoid false failures on slow CI.

steps.title: Wire enriched trace fields into JSON and Markdown report output
steps.description: Update `src/reporters/json-reporter.ts` to include the new trace telemetry in a top-level `diagnostics` key in the JSON report when the trace is available: seed breakdown, retrieval stats, confidence distribution, hypothesis stats, and AI summary. Update `src/reporters/markdown-reporter.ts` to add an optional 'Diagnostics' section at the bottom of the report that shows: pipeline step timings, seed count by category, finding confidence histogram (bucketed: 0-0.5, 0.5-0.75, 0.75-1.0), hypothesis conversion rate, and AI call stats (if AI was used). Gate the diagnostics section behind a `includeDiagnostics` option on the report builder. Update `src/reporters/report-builder.ts` to accept a `trace` parameter and thread it through. Add unit tests for the new diagnostics rendering in both reporters.

steps.title: Final integration pass: build, lint, and full test suite green
steps.description: Run the full build (`npm run build`) and verify all new and existing tests pass together. Fix any type errors, lint warnings, or test failures introduced by the previous steps. Ensure the new test files follow existing naming conventions (`__tests__/` directories, `.test.ts` suffix). Verify the enriched trace.json and scorecard output are valid JSON. Confirm that the `--debug` flag works end-to-end by running the built CLI against a test bundle. This step is the final validation gate.
